title: Implement Per-Device-Type Rate Limiting for VitalSync API
description: AetherCare VitalSync is a C-based REST API designed to ingest and process vital signs data from various medical IoT devices. Currently, the system enforces a single, global rate limit for all incoming data submissions, which is defined in the application configuration. This is inefficient as different devices have different data transmission frequencies (e.g., a continuous ECG monitor sends data far more frequently than a manual blood pressure cuff). This task requires implementing a more granular, per-device-type rate limiting system. The agent will need to modify the configuration, the core request handling logic, and the API's public contract over multiple sessions.

project_spec.name: AetherCare VitalSync
project_spec.description:
AetherCare VitalSync is a serverless REST and GraphQL API that allows clinics, tele-medicine providers, and personal health-device vendors to securely ingest, normalize, and query near-real-time patient vital-sign data (heart-rate, pulse-ox, glucose, blood-pressure, etc.). The platform exposes versioned REST endpoints for data upload, configuration management, and patient authorization flows, while a GraphQL façade offers fine-grained, cross-device querying and aggregation to clinicians’ dashboards.

Built entirely with custom C Lambda functions packaged in an AWS custom runtime, the service demonstrates how high-performance, low-footprint native binaries can be combined with cloud-native building blocks (API Gateway, DynamoDB, EventBridge, Cognito). The implementation uses strict request-validation schemas, pagination, and ranked rate-limiting tiers (per clinician, per device, per organization) enforced at the gateway. Repository Pattern abstracts DynamoDB and S3 persistence, while Command–Query Separation keeps mutation paths (device uploads, patient consents) distinct from analytical reads (GraphQL resolvers). Comprehensive logging, structured in JSON via AWS Embedded Metrics, enables traceability demanded by healthcare regulations such as HIPAA.

The project targets ~40 source/header/test/infra files (≈139 k tokens) and illustrates how a medium-sized, production-ready healthcare backend can be delivered with a purely serverless footprint, eliminating idle cost and simplifying compliance-driven scaling.
dependencies: AWS SDK for C (v3) – DynamoDB, S3, EventBridge, CloudWatch
libgraphqlparser – GraphQL query parsing and validation
libjwt – JWT creation/validation for Cognito integration
civetweb – lightweight HTTP client utilities for integration tests
